subject: Intercompany dataflow break-glass: transient cross-region handling & subprocessor traceability
messages:
From: Aarti Menon <aarti.menon@medicore.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Break-glass / transient cross-region processing question (MedicoRE)

Hi Neha,

Quick context: MedicoRE is finalizing our procurement checklist and need confirmation on one narrow item before we can sign the DPA. Our security team accepts region pinning in general, but they require explicit language around any "break-glass" transient cross-region processing used only for disaster recovery/failover. Specifically they asked: 

- Will Redwood ever spin up processing in another region for customer traffic outside of a documented failover window? 
- If so, can you provide the full subprocessor chain (who's involved) when that transient hop happens?
- What telemetry/log fields do you capture so we can audit no-data-exfiltration occurred during that event?

We attached our completed questionnaire (MedicoRE_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) with highlights on the residency fields.

We appreciate a concise reply we can include in our legal redlines. Procurement (procurement@medicore.com) is on the thread for timing.

Regards,
Aarti Menon
Head of Security & Compliance
MedicoRE

-----

Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Break-glass / transient cross-region processing question (MedicoRE)

Hi Aarti — thanks for the clear questions and for sending the questionnaire. Appreciate the detail.

High-level answer: Redwood's default commitment is region pinning for active processing (customer traffic stays within the pinned region). We do, however, operate a controlled break-glass mechanism for disaster recovery and capacity failover that can route requests to a compatible model variant in a secondary region under strictly defined conditions.

To make this actionable for your legal team, I propose we: 
1) Provide a short DPA addendum clause that defines the break-glass conditions and maximum duration.
2) Deliver a subprocessor roster for the break-glass pathway (who may be involved during such an event).
3) Share the telemetry schema and sample logs you can use to verify each transient event.

Marissa (legal) — can you draft the addendum language consistent with our standard temporary-hop model?
Jonas (infra) — can you confirm the technical constraints, expected windows (max time a request may leave the pinned region), and the log fields we can provide for audit?

Aarti — if you can confirm the minimum legal requirements (e.g., max duration, whether you need contractually-enforced notification SLA), we will prioritize this for your procurement timeline.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Aarti Menon <aarti.menon@medicore.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Break-glass / transient cross-region processing question (MedicoRE)

Hi Aarti / team — looping in legal.

We can accommodate a narrowly scoped DPA addendum that: 
- Defines break-glass as a declared incident (DR event, catastrophic capacity failure, or ordered regional evacuation).
- Limits transient cross-region processing to a maximum of 4 hours per declared event unless mutually agreed in writing.
- Requires Redwood to notify the customer within 1 hour of first cross-region activation and provide a post-event audit report within 72 hours.

We will attach the proposed clause as redlines to the DPA draft Neha uploaded. Please note we can provide a subprocessor roster for the break-glass pathway, but that roster may include third-party cloud providers and our managed infra partners — we will list company names and their service roles. We cannot, for confidentiality, provide certain vendor contract exhibits, but we can provide attestations and the full subprocessor names/locations.

Action items for MedicoRE to confirm: 
- Is 4 hours acceptable as a max duration?
- Do you require a statutory-level indemnity for break-glass traffic (we typically do not accept unlimited indemnities).
- Any mandatory data residency language your counsel needs in the DPA addendum (exact phrasing)?

If you send a target clause or redlines, we'll respond quickly.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Break-glass / transient cross-region processing question (MedicoRE)

Hi all — technical detail from infra. Short version first: transient hops are limited, instrumented, and only used when regional capacity/reliability is compromised. Below are the operational guarantees we can provide and the telemetry fields we will deliver for audits.

Operational guarantees (we commit in practice and can reflect in an addendum):
- Scope: Only read/write inference traffic (not backups or non-request telemetry) is eligible for transient routing.
- Trigger conditions: manual DR declaration by Redwood on-call or automated failure thresholds (multi-AZ regional control-plane loss). Trigger will be documented per-incident.
- Max duration: by default 4 hours per incident; can be extended by mutual written agreement.
- Limit: We will not proactively route steady-state customer traffic across regions for cost or performance reasons.

Subprocessor chain (high level; we will provide a roster):
- Primary region provider: (e.g., Azure EU-West / AWS us-west-2) — cloud infra provider
- Network partner: CDN / edge partner (if edge hop used)
- Managed infra partner: our capacity provider for dedicated pools

Telemetry / audit fields (we can provide logs and a sample CSV/JSON per incident):
- request_id: unique per request
- customer_tenant_id: your tenant identifier
- original_region: region that received the request
- active_region: region that processed the request during the event
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- model_variant: model name + version used for processing
- bytes_in/bytes_out: token-size metrics (aggregated)
- egress_flag: boolean if data left pinned region
- trigger_type: manual|auto
- operator_id: on-call operator who declared the event

Retention & delivery: we retain the incident logs for 13 months by default for post-incident audit and can deliver a filtered export (redacted where appropriate) within 72 hours of request.

Attached is a small telemetry schema stub you can drop into your SOC team review.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
